correctness.rationale: The positive adult mean is sb/(1-m). Eliminating juvenile abundance yields a stable AR(2) equation with coefficients h and m-h, and white innovation variance s²v_J+v_A. Three Yule–Walker equations yield the exact stationary CV². Half the derivative of log CV² equals T_m(y)-q/[y(y²+q)]. The derivative of Q_m factors as y²(1+y)(1+m-2y)H_m/D_m²; H_m=(1-m)(z+2)-3z³>0 because z=1-y<=sqrt(1-m). This proves unique global minimization and yields the endpoint q_c=m⁴/(1-2m²) if m<1/sqrt(2), with boundary equality included. No finite grid is used to prove infinite uniqueness. Exact-rational script verified 57,978 supplementary assertions.

originality.rationale: The searched accessible scientific sources cover deterministic selective fishery delay dynamics, general structured stochastic covariance, and transfer functions; the most directly equivalent published AR(2) optimizer covers only fixed innovation variance and the q=0 special case, which is explicitly not claimed. The q>0 competing-noise model has policy-dependent innovation variance and stationary mean, and the global necessary-sufficient boundary was not identified in inspected results. This is a bounded historical originality assessment, not an independent novelty certificate.

value.rationale: Two independently fluctuating age stages are biologically motivated sources of population risk. Fixing the demographic replacement margin while changing the stage allocation isolates a natural risk mechanism. The exact necessary/sufficient boundary and unique interior optimizer distinguish whether adult retention should be zero or positive without relying on an arbitrary numerical slice. This gives a structural management-model insight and a sharp design principle within the specified response approximation, without claiming field calibration.
